symptom: `create workflow … call workflow M.Child … boundary event interrupting timer … { … };` fails to parse ("mismatched input 'boundary' expecting ';'", "mismatched input 'interrupting' expecting SUBPROCESS") while the identical clause after `call microflow` / `wait for notification` parses. DESCRIBE of a workflow whose call-workflow activity has a timer (Studio Pro-authored, or added by ALTER `insert into callX { boundary event … }`) prints that clause, so its describe output did not re-parse
cause: `workflowCallWorkflowStmt` (MDLWorkflow.g4) had no BOUNDARY EVENT clause and `ast.WorkflowCallWorkflowNode` no BoundaryEvents field, though the reader, writer, describer, ALTER mutator and MCP backend all handled Workflows$CallWorkflowActivity.boundaryEvents (10.14+, the same floor as every other owner). None of the AST walkers knew the case either: seven hand-written switches over the boundary-event owners (walkWorkflowActivities, collectEndBodies, the WF07 bare-timer count, WF15, the WF19 sites, the rewrite-guard count, the notification gate) listed user task / call microflow / wait only. Two SDK walkers had the same gap on the stored side: collectStoredPlacements (ALTER end ancestry lost the non-interrupting context under a call workflow) and collectJumpableNames (MDL-WF05 did not see activities inside a call-workflow boundary body)
fix: Grammar reuses call microflow's exact boundary clause (no new tokens); the visitor fills BoundaryEvents; buildCallWorkflowActivity writes them through buildBoundaryEvents. A new executor helper, workflowActivityBoundaryEvents, is the one place that lists the AST owners; the walkers that only need the events go through it, and the two that label by owner (WF15, WF19) gained the case. The stored walkers gained the CallWorkflowActivity case
file: mdl/grammar/domains/MDLWorkflow.g4; mdl/ast/ast_workflow.go; mdl/visitor/visitor_workflow.go; mdl/executor/cmd_workflows_write.go, validate_workflow.go (workflowActivityBoundaryEvents), validate_workflow_end.go, validate_workflow_esp.go, validate_workflow_scope.go, validate_workflow_refs.go, validate_workflow_rewrite.go, validate_workflow_jump.go; tests mdl/visitor/visitor_workflow_callworkflow_boundary_test.go, mdl/executor/workflow_callworkflow_boundary_test.go; mdl-examples/bug-tests/1532-call-workflow-boundary-events.mdl
insight: When the read side, describe and ALTER all handle a property and only CREATE cannot spell it, the gap is a round-trip break, not a missing feature: describe output is the repro. The grammar line was one; the cost was the walkers. Every rule that recurses into boundary bodies had its own owner switch, and adding an owner meant finding all of them: grep for the node types of the EXISTING owners (e.g. WorkflowWaitForNotificationNode), not the new one, since the new one appears in none of the switches that are wrong. Folding them onto one helper keeps the next owner from repeating it. Revert controls were per walker: each rule row failed only with its own walker reverted, which shows each case is load-bearing. Measured: interrupting and non-interrupting timer on call workflow, mx check 0 errors on 11.6.6 and 11.15.0, describe -> exec 'already in sync' on both
